summary: The lecture introduces the Indian Economy NCERT series (Class 6-12), emphasizing introductory macroeconomics over microeconomics for UPSC. It defines economy as three core economic activities—production, consumption, distribution—within a territory. It distinguishes economic vs non-economic activities, explains goods vs services, and details the three-sector classification: primary (agriculture, mining), secondary (manufacturing, construction, utilities), tertiary (services). India is noted as a service-based economy with ~55% output from services.
points: UPSC Prelims: ~15 economics questions/year since 2013; only 2 from microeconomics, both basic.
UPSC Mains: 8 economics questions/year, exclusively on Indian economy issues, no concept-based questions.
60% Prelims economics questions on Indian economy issues; 40-50% on applied macroeconomics.
Economic activity: work done for money or money's worth; non-economic activity: work for other considerations (love, duty).
Production: extraction/transformation of natural resources → goods (tangible, storable) and services (intangible, non-storable, consumed at production).
Consumption: using output of production with monetary value; distribution: exchange via markets moving goods/services from producers to consumers.
Economy: production, consumption, distribution associated with a specific territory.
Primary sector: agriculture & allied (crops, livestock, fisheries, forestry) + mining & quarrying; output = natural products/raw materials.
Secondary sector: manufacturing, construction, utilities (water, electricity, fuel); transforms primary output into finished goods.
Tertiary sector: services (education, healthcare, banking, trade, transport, communication, public admin); supports primary/secondary sectors.
India: service-based economy; services contribute ~55% of total output.
